svg.title: Conditional terminal incidence tests
svg.desc: Actual terminal T multiplicity space has dimension three. A canonical nonzero functional defines a dimension two kernel plane. The residual mechanism requires its dimension one terminal multiplicity line to lie in that plane for the fourth lift to vanish. The separated mechanism requires equality of its dimension two terminal plane with the canonical plane. These are unselected incidence tests, not selected positions or completion fractions.

g.text: T-multiplicity ambient space: C³ · canonical nonzero ℓ · C_term = ker ℓ (plane, dimension 2)
Projectively in P²: point lies on line
F5 = 2T · actual dimension 12 (may be a graph)
Vector multiplicities: equality of dimension-2 planes
Projectively in P²: equality of lines
Neither incidence is selected. These are tests, not actual plotted positions or probabilities.
PR1097: residual-large has β = 0, α possibly zero; no analogous nonzero-N0 restriction.
PR1101: separated τ = 0 forces R ≠ 0; if τ ≠ 0, zero requires the unique graph −τ⁻¹ℓ0.
PR1094 · No completion percentage. C_term is unrelated to the opposite-pencil cokernel C.
